item.title: SCP-XXXX (Gestalt Suffering)
item.content:encoded:
Foundation personnel encounter anomalous bio-hazard which rewrites the memories of exposed individuals.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article w/ GRU-P GoI Formats As well

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch:
- SCP-XXXX is a contagious biohazard developed by GRU-P as a mass amnestic to be deployed against target populations in conjunction with large scale cognitohazardous propaganda campaigns.
- SCP-XXXX does not produce the intended affect, instead, all individuals exposed to SCP-XXXX have memories and personality traits changed at random, developing personality traits and memories of other individuals afflicted by SCP-XXXX, living or dead.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
Foundation Personnel are initially unaware of the anomalous properties of SCP-XXXX when it is first encountered, instead mistaking it for a conventional biohazard developed by Soviet Researchers at Aralsk-7/Vozrozhdeniya Island. After several incidents, however, Special Containment Procedures are developed. The discovery and containment of SCP-XXXX will be told thru interviews and incident reports focusing on the mental and emotional challenges Foundation Personnel must overcome, particularly the afflicted, who are able to observe and experience the destruction of their identities without knowing exactly what is going on.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Due to the proliferation of chemical and biological weapons at former Soviet Weapons Site/GRU-P installation Aralsk-7, discovery and containment is a unique challenge for the Foundation due to risks posed by other SCP’s at that location as well as conventional hazards and the involvement of other GoI’s (Namely UN/GOC). Story will have heavy focus on the tragedy which sometimes befalls Foundation Personnel in the pursuit of their mission.

Additional Notes:
Would love advice on formatting as well as dramatic storytelling through otherwise clinical Foundation interviews and incident reports. Also, any guidance on GRU-P formatting/storytelling also welcome. Thanks!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn
